Rules / Cleanup

SK0243 The qualifier is redundant

A namespace- or type-qualified type name the simple name already binds to, or a base. that reaches the same member as no qualifier.

CategoryCleanup
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0
SupersedesRedundantBaseQualifier

Why

A qualifier is how a reader is told that the short name would have meant something else, so one that changes nothing is a false signal: System.Text.StringBuilder beside a using System.Text; says there is an ambiguity to resolve, and there is not. base. says louder still — it says the containing type has its own member of that name and this call deliberately goes past it. SK0207 owns the this. qualifier and SK0215 the static one; these are the two shapes the arrangement rules leave.

Example

Instead of:

using System.Text;

sealed class Formatter {
    System.Text.StringBuilder builder = new();
}

Write:

using System.Text;

sealed class Formatter {
    StringBuilder builder = new();
}

When it does not fire

⚠ Neither half is decided by comparing text. The type half asks the semantic model to bind the short name at the same position and reports only when it produces the same symbol with no candidates, which is what makes a shadowing type, a missing using directive and a genuine ambiguity each answer for themselves. Deciding it by looking for a matching using directive would be a different rule, and it would be wrong every time two imported namespaces offer the same name. ⚠ The `base.` half is not "the containing type does not override it", and believing that is how this rule would report a behaviour change as a redundancy. Given class A { public virtual void M() { } }, a class B : A calling base.M(), and a class C : B that overrides M — dropping the qualifier in B turns a non-virtual call to A.M into a virtual one that reaches C.M. So the member must be one nothing can override further (not virtual, not abstract, not an unsealed override) or the containing type must be sealed. Two further conditions: the containing type must declare nothing of that name, and nothing in scope at that position may be a local, a parameter or a local function of that name, because an unqualified use would find it first. ⚠ An attribute name is left out. [System.Obsolete] binds to a constructor rather than to a type, so the symbol comparison the rest of the rule performs would be comparing the wrong things; the shape is real and it is declined rather than answered with a check that does not mean what it says. ⚠ global:: is a deliberate disambiguator and is never removed — a short name that binds to the same symbol today is exactly what somebody wrote global:: to stop depending on. A qualified name inside another one's type arguments is skipped too, because the outer finding and the inner one would be two overlapping edits, and two overlapping edits are not a fix. Using directives, namespace declarations and documentation crefs are all positions where the written name is the meaning. ⚠ `UnusedImportClause` belongs to `SK0210`, not here, and so does RedundantUsingDirective.Global — see the note against SK0210 in docs/plan/08: its removal set is Roslyn's CS8019, and the global-duplication shape reports CS8933, which that filter does not read. Shipping it here would have been a second rule for one concept.
